headline: Five injured by gunfire on way to wedding event in Noakhali
summary: Five people, including an event cameraman, were shot by miscreants while traveling to a 'gaye holud' ceremony in Noakhali. One victim is in critical condition and has been transferred to Dhaka for advanced treatment.
details: Five individuals, including an event management cameraman, were shot by miscreants in Noakhali's Begumganj upazila. The incident occurred around 11:15 PM on Monday, August 18, in the Gazitola area of Alaipur Union's Moushakpur village.

The victims, identified as Nazrul Islam Shanto, Maruf Ahammed, Jasim Uddin, Sakib Hossain, and Bablu, were traveling in three motorcycles and two CNGs to video a 'gaye holud' event. They claim miscreants fired indiscriminately at them from behind.
One of the injured is in critical condition and has been sent to Dhaka for advanced medical care. The others are currently receiving treatment at Noakhali General Hospital.

Victim Nazrul Islam identified local individuals Harun and Picchi Riyad among the attackers. Locals, however, suggest the attack stemmed from a pre-existing dispute. Police have stated they will investigate the incident and take legal action.

headline: Mother arrested for drowning 14-day-old child in Noakhali, police say
summary: Police in Noakhali recovered the body of a 14-day-old infant from a plastic water drum. The mother has been arrested and reportedly confessed, citing the baby's constant crying as the motive.
details: Police recovered the body of a 14-day-old infant from a plastic water drum in Begumganj, Noakhali, on Monday night. The baby's mother, Fatema Begum, has been arrested in connection with the incident.
The infant was the son of Sourav Hossain and Fatema Begum, residents of Majumderhat area. The couple married in November last year, and Fatema gave birth to the child on August 4.

Family members began searching for the baby after he went missing on Monday evening. When questioned, Fatema gave inconsistent statements, initially claiming someone took the child or that "jinn" had taken him.
Suspicious of her contradictory remarks, family members intensified their search and eventually found the infant's body in a drum used for collecting rainwater.

Police reported that Fatema Begum confessed to drowning her child in the drum. She stated that the baby's continuous crying prevented her from sleeping, leading her to commit the act out of frustration.

Md. Shamsuzzaman, Officer-in-Charge of Begumganj Police Station, confirmed Fatema Begum is in police custody. He added that legal action would be taken following an investigation, and the family has been asked to file a written complaint.
